## Natural history notes

A small long-legged fly characterized by its metallic green thorax, dark central stripe, slender body, long legs, and clear wings. In Florida, it is found in warm, humid habitats such as gardens, forest edges, parks, wetlands, yards, and other areas with vegetation and small arthropod prey. Adults are agile predators that run and fly across leaves, stems, and shaded surfaces while hunting tiny insects, while the larvae likely develop in moist soil, leaf litter, or decaying organic material where they prey on small invertebrates.
